title: Cost-sensitivity fingerprinting and progressive acceptance for batch/cache auto-applies
creator: Aisha Malik
description:
Goal: Build a deterministic evaluation and rollout mechanism that prevents quality regressions when the cost optimizer recommends batch/cache config changes. We will attach a per-workload 'cost-sensitivity fingerprint' that quantifies how sensitive outputs are to batching and KV cache changes across model variants, sequence-length distributions, and prompt archetypes.

Scope & deliverables:
- Fingerprint generator: offline profiling job that runs a representative prompt corpus across: model variants (int8/qat/fp16), sequence buckets (0-128,129-512,>512), and batch sizes / KV cache states. Outputs: per-prompt delta metrics (embedding cosine, token-level perplexity delta, hallucination flags, task-specific accuracy where applicable).
- Stratified golden prompt set: curate anchor sets per customer/workload cluster (50-200 golden prompts) with metadata (expected intent, critical spans, acceptance tolerance). These are used for both automatic gating and periodic human audits.
- Acceptance criteria: define non-inferiority margins per fingerprint using embedding-similarity distributions and task-specific thresholds. Default policy: require (a) mean embedding similarity >= 0.985 for high-sensitivity fingerprints or >= 0.96 for low-sensitivity; (b) human-audited regression rate < 1% on sampled outputs; (c) throughput/cost improvements > 6% to trigger auto-apply. Statistical test: two-sided bootstrap CI on median cosine with pre-specified non-inferiority delta.
- Progressive acceptance & rollout stages: shadow -> canary (1%) -> ramp (10% / 50% / 100%) with automated hold/rollback triggers based on real-time sentinel checks (semantic drift, error-rate spike, latency regressions).
- Integration points: console dashboards (per-customer fingerprint view), rollout orchestration (policy engine), audit workflow (human-in-the-loop sampling), and PR pipeline for any autotune policy changes.
- Runbook & rollback: explicit rollback conditions (embedding drop > delta AND human-audit confirm OR customer complaint rate > threshold). Automations must capture and persist failing examples to S3 and open a ticket with linked artifacts.

Trade-offs & rationale:
- Use embedding-based metrics (OpenAI/SimCSE-style embeddings) as primary automatic signal because they capture semantic drift better than surface overlap; supplement with task-specific metrics where available (e.g., QA F1).
- Conservative default thresholds to avoid brittle auto-applies for high-sensitivity workloads; allow customers to opt-in to more aggressive cost-first policies.
- Compute cost of fingerprinting: schedule offline profiling on spot/low-priority nodes and cache fingerprints; update frequency default monthly or after major model change.

Acceptance criteria for this ticket:
1) Fingerprint generator implemented and validated on two representative tenant clusters (documentation of profiles and stored artifacts).
2) Golden prompt curator UI prototype and export format implemented in console (CSV + metadata).
3) Automated gating pipeline created with at least one non-inferiority statistical test and canary rollout policy wired to the deployment controller.
4) Runbook and sample dashboard panels published, plus an example rollback triggered in staging.

Links & artifacts:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Cost+Sensitivity+Fingerprinting
- Prototype repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/autotune-fingerprint (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/autotune-fingerprint/pull/12)
- Orchestration PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/realtime/pull/6789
- Staging dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/8aBcS/cost-sensitivity-staging

Notes on customer privacy: fingerprints must not include PII. All recorded examples used for human audits must be redacted and stored in the customer-specific bucket with appropriate IAM.
comments: 2025-02-10 - Aisha Malik: Created ticket. Initial sketch posted to confluence; flagged as dependency for rollout engine work.

2025-02-12 - Evan Chen: Completed prototype of offline profiler for 3 model variants. Initial results show ~8-12% cost win for many mid-length prompts; however prompts in the legal cluster experience small factuality degradation—requires stricter thresholds.

2025-02-14 - Design review (Lina Park): Recommended addition of a 'critical-span' label in golden prompts so human auditors can focus on safety/requirements-sensitive tokens. Filed DES-402 for console UI work.
2025-02-16 - QA (Marco): Implemented bootstrap test harness; found a seasonal bias in our sampling that underweights long-sequence >512 cases. Updated profiler to stratify by sequence-length buckets.

2025-02-17 - Evan Chen: Wired canary pipeline to deployment controller in staging. Canary held at 1% automatically due to embedding similarity dipping to 0.961 for one tenant; created a rollback candidate artifact and opened ENG-155002 to investigate model-kernel interaction.
2025-02-18 - Aisha Malik: Scheduled human audit for flagged canary outputs (5 auditors). Next steps: finalize acceptance thresholds and publish runbook.
